subsystems.name: Collector swarm
subsystems.role: vast numbers of independent solar collectors orbiting the star, rather than one solid shell — the form proposed by Freeman Dyson in 1960.
parts: station-keeping thrusters or light-pressure attitude control

subsystems.name: Orbital infrastructure
subsystems.role: moves mass and people cheaply around the system.
parts: orbital rings or launch loops (speculative, dynamically supported)

subsystems.name: Resource and manufacturing base
subsystems.role: turns asteroidal and planetary rock into more collectors.

subsystems.name: Power transmission
subsystems.role: gets energy from the swarm to where it is used.

subsystems.name: Habitation
subsystems.role: keeps a civilisation alive while it builds.

subsystems.name: Thermal management
subsystems.role: radiates the waste heat that any energy-harvesting structure must shed.

buildSteps.title: Survey the system
buildSteps.detail: Telescopes and probes map water, metals and carbon across asteroids, moons and the star's inner planets — the raw material budget.

buildSteps.title: Establish off-world industry
buildSteps.detail: Automated mining, refining and a mass driver or electromagnetic launcher put material into orbit without chemical rockets.

buildSteps.title: Bootstrap self-replicating manufacturing
buildSteps.detail: Factories that build more factories from local material, so the industrial base grows without shipments from Earth.

buildSteps.title: Deploy the first collectors
buildSteps.detail: A small swarm of solar-thermal or photovoltaic units is placed in orbits chosen to avoid shading each other.

buildSteps.title: Grow the swarm incrementally
buildSteps.detail: Each generation of collectors powers the mining and manufacturing of the next; coverage rises over decades to millennia.

buildSteps.title: Build orbital rings and launch loops
buildSteps.detail: Moving-mass structures provide fixed platforms in orbit and cut the cost of lifting further material.

buildSteps.title: Assemble habitats
buildSteps.detail: Rotating pressurised settlements house the population and industry that keep the swarm running.

buildSteps.title: Beam and distribute power
buildSteps.detail: Microwave or laser links deliver energy to habitats and outbound spacecraft.

buildSteps.title: Manage heat
buildSteps.detail: Radiators dump waste heat; the infrared glow is the signature astronomers actually search for.

prerequisites.why: reusable rockets have cut launch costs, but the mass a star-scale project needs is orders of magnitude beyond current traffic.
a swarm must largely build itself from local material, since shipping it from Earth is impossible.
asteroid and lunar mining has been demonstrated only at laboratory and small-demonstration scale.
microwave and laser power transfer has been demonstrated over kilometres, not interplanetary distances.
space stations recycle some air and water, but no artificial ecosystem has run unaided for years.
orbital rings need structural materials and active mass streams far beyond any built today.

pathway.milestone: orbital habitats and in-space manufacturing demonstrations
pathway.unlocks: experience of living and working off Earth for long periods.

pathway.milestone: asteroid and lunar mining feeding orbital industry
pathway.unlocks: material supply that does not depend on Earth launches.

pathway.milestone: self-replicating factories building a growing collector swarm
pathway.unlocks: exponential growth toward a significant fraction of a star's output, known as a Kardashev Type II civilisation.

pathway.milestone: orbital rings, habitats and power beaming at system scale
pathway.unlocks: a permanently space-based civilisation whose infrared glow would be detectable by distant astronomers.
